predecessors.name: Copán
predecessors.text: Quiriguá, Izabal Department, 'covering approximately 3 square kilometres', on the Motagua River jade route

ledger.x: 426: 'The recorded history of Quiriguá starts in 426': K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' became king of Copán and three days later set up Tok Casper as Quiriguá's first known king.
426: 'right from the beginning of its recorded history Quiriguá was subservient to its southern neighbour' Copán; the city was placed to put the Motagua trade route under Copán's control.

May 738: K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat 'captured the powerful, but elderly 13th king of Copán', Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil, who 'on 3 May 738 ... was decapitated in a public ritual'; Quiriguá 'retained its independence from Copán'.
810: 'the last hieroglyphic texts were raised at Quiriguá'; 'within a few years Quiriguá was all but deserted' ('All construction had halted by about 850').

wars.name: Quiriguá's rebellion against Copán
wars.outcome: In 736 K'ak' Tiliw received a visit from Wamaw K'awiil of Calakmul, which 'strongly suggests that Calakmul sponsored Quiriguá's rebellion in order to weaken Tikal'; in 738 he captured and beheaded Copán's king (3 May 738).
